purpose: Keep the tools page calm, local-first, and easy to scan on desktop and touch screens.

referenceHierarchy.use: Primary visual source of truth: editorial hierarchy, neutral canvas, restrained semantic accents.
Audit lens: explicit hierarchy, consistent tokens, anti-slop restraint, and a clear reason for every visual element.
Mobile reference only: health states should be legible, quiet when normal, and obvious when attention is needed.
Interaction reference: use transform and opacity for short feedback, and always honor reduced motion.
Pattern reference only: borrow soft aurora background movement, spotlight response, and card composition ideas without adding a React dependency.
Interaction reference for right-click / long-press menu anatomy, collision-aware placement, dismissal, focus, and keyboard navigation; implemented locally in vanilla JS.
Implementation source for hierarchical 3D transforms on ordinary DOM elements; the existing HTML buttons remain the accessible interaction authority.
Pattern reference for interactive 3D panels, nested surfaces, depth, and button feedback; adapted to the project's vanilla HTML/CSS surface instead of replacing business controls with canvas text.
Implementation source for the small desktop companion's spring/inertia cursor following; the body and eyes are local project pixel sprites.

implementation.css3dPanels: CSS3DRenderer-inspired DOM panel controller; each real tool button owns its perspective, extrusion, pointer tilt, sheen, focus depth, and pressed state
implementation.mousePet: local adapted MIT mouse-follower spring/inertia behavior with the original local ghost sprite style
implementation.motion: bounded archive-field spotlight plus short transform and opacity transitions
implementation.upperField: Use the side whitespace for quiet, source-derived rails and a small route map; do not stretch the hero to fill it.
implementation.archiveField: A low-contrast radial contour field, asymmetrical shell, route line, and shared pointer light visually connect the two operation surfaces without adding a separate 3D object.
implementation.archiveCore: Export remains a separate one-off operation. Archive Health owns Sync and Data Check as one connected surface, while Movement Dictionary remains a separate reference entry. No detached model is placed inside a card; pointer and focus state move the complete semantic button as one shallow layered panel.
implementation.globalPet: The original tartan ghost is mounted once at app startup. Right-click, Context Menu key, or Shift+F10 opens a collision-aware local route menu for every top-level interface and utility route.
implementation.dataPolicy: derive visual status from existing state; never invent health or sync data

constraints: Do not change Analysis Export or Movement Dictionary protocol semantics; Cloud Sync and Data Health protocols remain unchanged while their presentation is redesigned.
Do not add a second source of truth or copy formal data into the worktree.
Do not add remote runtime dependencies; copied open-source assets must be local, license-documented, and scoped to Tools.
The page title must name the utility surface; do not replace it with a campaign-style slogan.
Do not pair oversized display type with explanatory microcopy unless it clarifies a real action.
Use rounded pills only for real status or navigation; never as decorative labels.
Hover feedback may use color, border, or spotlight; do not lift every card by default.
Decorative marks must explain the archive surface or its three routes; no invented status, badges, or visual filler.
The background field must connect the panels visually without becoming a second content layer or changing semantic state.
Keep primary actions keyboard reachable with visible focus styles.
Keep the page usable at narrow widths and disable decorative motion for prefers-reduced-motion.
acceptance: Export and Archive Health remain the two primary operation surfaces; Sync and Data Check remain reachable through their current data-tools-panel hooks, and Movement Dictionary stays a separate reference entry.
Desktop reads as one maintenance desk with a clear primary action.
Mobile stacks the same content without horizontal overflow and preserves touch target size.
Visual motion is non-blocking and uses only transform, opacity, or a bounded background spotlight.
The CSS3D layer enhances the real HTML buttons, cleans up on route changes, and degrades to a static accessible surface on touch and reduced-motion contexts.
The original ghost remains available across all routes, and its context menu reaches the existing navigation routes without introducing a second router.
